source.title: Letting Claude do Autonomous Research to Improve SAEs

page_placements.theme: Encoder inference and optimization affect feature recovery

record.tranche_reason: The post uses a synthetic SAE benchmark that includes feature superposition to improve SAE performance, but does not test the claim's proposed superposition geometry, capacity account, or LLM representation claims.
record.gate_note: The post reports aggregate SAE feature-recovery scores on SynthSAEBench-16k, which is a synthetic setting rather than an LLM. These results do not measure whether features are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, how sparsity or importance changes the geometry, or whether SAE features are canonical units. The LLM discussion reports inconclusive validation rather than claim-specific outcomes.
record.test_reason: The post optimizes SAE architectures on a synthetic benchmark (SynthSAEBench-16k) built to include superposition. It reports only its own method's F1/MCC gains, not whether features are superposed, how geometry varies, or whether SAE features are canonical units in a model. The LLM validation is reported as inconclusive, with no numbers.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. Claude's autonomous research raised F1 and MCC on the single synthetic benchmark. The author warns the gains may reflect hill-climbing on that model. On LLMs, LISTA with eta=0.3 seems to break and other results are indistinguishable from noise.
record.recipe_differences: The post optimizes SAE performance on SynthSAEBench-16k; it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition method or measure its proposed geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: On the synthetic benchmark, the authors report that a single LISTA iteration with adjustment weighting 0.3 performed best. More than 3 iterations, learning the weighting, or learning multiple encoder parameters reportedly led to overfitting and poorer tracking of ground-truth features. For LLM SAEs, LISTA with eta=0.3 seemed to break, while lower eta results were difficult to distinguish from noise.

fits_no_version.finding: On SynthSAEBench-16k at L0=25, a LISTA-Matryoshka SAE (4096 latents, 16k ground-truth features) reached F1 0.97 and MCC 0.84, versus the best prior SAE at 0.88 and 0.78. The author suspects overfitting to this one synthetic model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE encoder refinements (e.g., one-step LISTA) improve ground-truth feature recovery on a synthetic superposition benchmark; transfer to LLMs is unverified.

record.problems: The reported gains are on a single synthetic model and the author suspects over-optimization to it. No uncertainty estimates or multiple-seed results are reported for the headline scores. The author says LLM SAEBench metrics are noisy, results can point in different directions, and the LLM validation has not established a decisive improvement.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant results were reported. Per-component score changes are not given numerically; LLM validation is described as inconclusive without claim-specific metric values.

untested.parts: All: geometry, sparsity transition and near-orthogonality are not measured; superposition is built into the benchmark by design.
SAE recovery of sparse features in LLMs: attempted but reported only as inconclusive or noisy, with no values.
Completeness, stability and canonicity of SAE features are not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Superposition is a design feature of the benchmark rather than an object of measurement. No uncertainty or multiple-seed results are reported. Comments report another agent's F1 of 0.989, not part of the post's own results.

versions.untested_parts: Whether sparse features in an overcomplete toy network are stored as overlapping, nearly orthogonal directions, and how sparsity affects transitions or geometry.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons can arise without capacity pressure.
Whether LLMs spread features across neurons or whether SAEs recover sparse features in LLMs.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of a model's representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.
